steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: A just war is a war that meets specific moral criteria. A holy war is fought for religious reasons or on God's command. They are different concepts — a war can be one without being the other. | RS Exam Tips — Just War and Holy War: 1. For Just War and Holy War questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Just War and Holy War to its real-world impact on believers and society | UK Context: In the UK, debates about often involve both religious and secular voices. Parliament considers evidence

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain the Just War theory and how it compares to Islamic teachings on war.
